articles.title: Amazon Raises Its India Bet to $48 Billion. That Is More Than Most Countries Spend on AI.
articles.excerpt: A fresh $13 billion for data centres in Mumbai and Hyderabad puts AWS at the centre of a hyperscaler land grab that Google and Microsoft are already waging across the subcontinent.
articles.image_caption: An Amazon Web Services data centre facility in the western United States
articles.nri_angle: The hyperscaler investment wave creates thousands of cloud and AI jobs in India while deepening the cross-border career pathways that Indian-American tech professionals depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Indian-Origin Companies Just Struck a $310 Million Deal for the Unsexy Work That Makes AI Actually Function
articles.excerpt: EXL's acquisition of iMerit brings together Indian-diaspora-led data analytics and AI model training into one company that covers the full pipeline from data labelling to enterprise deployment.
articles.image_caption: A 3D visualization of neural network connections representing AI data infrastructure
articles.nri_angle: Both EXL and iMerit are led by Indian-origin founders and employ thousands across India and the US — the deal shows diaspora companies shaping the AI data value chain, not just consuming it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Is Putting AI Agents Inside American Hospitals. The Proving Ground Is a Virginia Health System.
articles.excerpt: India's second-largest IT firm deploys its Topaz Fabric agentic platform across Sentara's hospital operations, betting that healthcare is where enterprise AI either earns trust or loses it.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers at Infosys are building production-grade AI systems for regulated American healthcare — a shift from legacy IT services that redefines what Indian tech talent does in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian-Origin Leaders Will Now Help Reshape the Federal Reserve. One of Them Ran India's Central Bank.
articles.excerpt: Raghuram Rajan, Raj Chetty, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma have been named to lead three of five task forces reviewing how the world's most powerful central bank operates.
articles.image_caption: Raghuram Rajan, former Reserve Bank of India governor, now leads a Federal Reserve balance sheet policy task force
articles.nri_angle: Three Indian Americans now sit at the table where US monetary policy is being redesigned — from balance sheet strategy to AI's impact on jobs — a historic concentration of diaspora influence at the Fed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Cleared a Chinese Smartphone Giant to Build Phones Under Indian Ownership. It Took 18 Months.
articles.excerpt: Dixon Technologies will hold 51 per cent of a new joint venture with Vivo, the first major China-India manufacturing partnership approved since the border standoff reshaped investment rules.
articles.image_caption: Vivo, the Chinese smartphone giant, will operate in India through a joint venture with Dixon Technologies under Indian majority ownership (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The approval reshapes the India-China tech manufacturing relationship that NRIs and Indian investors have watched warily since 2020 — and positions Dixon as a potential portfolio play for diaspora investors betting on Make in India electronics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Picked 20 Indian AI Startups for Its Accelerator. A New York VC Dropped $100 Million to Bet on More.
articles.excerpt: From healthcare to climate tech, India's AI startup pipeline is attracting institutional backing from both Silicon Valley and the Indian-American investor class — with agentic AI and physical AI systems leading the new wave.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American VCs and tech executives are increasingly channelling capital back into India's AI ecosystem — and Google's accelerator pipeline offers NRI founders a structured path to scale globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Now Opens a Global Capability Centre Every Single Day. Nestlé Just Signed Up.
articles.excerpt: With 2,100 centres, 2.3 million workers, and $100 billion in annual revenue, India's GCC empire is growing faster than any outsourcing model before it — but AI threatens to rewrite the playbook.
articles.image_caption: HITEC City in Hyderabad, one of India's major tech hubs hosting global capability centres (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs at US tech giants increasingly collaborate with — or consider moving to — India's booming GCC centres, where leadership roles now mirror headquarters and the talent pipeline runs both ways.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Committed $30 Billion to Make Chips in America. Indian Engineers Will Design Most of Them.
articles.excerpt: The biggest manufacturing commitment in Apple's history deepens its partnership with Broadcom and signals a new era of US-made silicon — powered largely by immigrant talent.
articles.image_caption: Apple CEO Tim Cook, who called the Broadcom agreement the company's largest domestic manufacturing commitment
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a significant share of chip design teams at both Apple and Broadcom. This deal expands the semiconductor jobs pipeline that has drawn Indian talent to the US for decades.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Wants to Give the US Government a $42 Billion Stake. An Indian American Is Helping Broker the Deal.
articles.excerpt: Sam Altman's proposal to hand 5 per cent of OpenAI's equity to a public wealth fund could reshape how America profits from AI — and Sriram Krishnan, the White House's AI policy chief, is at the centre of it.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who has championed the concept of a public wealth fund tied to AI equity
articles.nri_angle: Sriram Krishnan, an Indian-American tech executive, serves as the White House's AI policy advisor and sits at the nexus of the government-industry negotiations that will shape how AI wealth is distributed to the American public.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Samsung Minted a Record $58.5 Billion in Profit. Wall Street Dumped the Stock.
articles.excerpt: The biggest quarter in memory-chip history triggered a global semiconductor selloff. Two days later, SK Hynix pulled off America's largest foreign IPO. The AI trade is not dead — but it is getting expensive.
articles.image_caption: Samsung Electronics headquarters (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian Americans work at Nvidia, Intel, Micron, AMD and Qualcomm — the companies whose stocks whipsawed this week. For NRIs with concentrated tech portfolios, the sell-the-news rotation is a reminder that the AI memory trade requires more discipline than conviction.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Major AI Lab Is Racing to Sign an Indian IT Giant. The $315 Billion Industry's Survival Depends on It.
articles.excerpt: TCS partnered with Anthropic and Mistral in six weeks. Infosys and HCLTech signed their own deals. The frontier AI labs need enterprise distributors. India's IT firms need a reason to exist. It is a marriage of mutual desperation — and it might just work.
articles.image_caption: Infosys campus in Bengaluru — one of India's IT giants racing to partner with AI labs (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For the hundreds of thousands of Indian tech professionals in the US and UK — many at TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech — the AI partnership race will determine whether their employers reinvent or decline. The premium is shifting from coding volume to AI orchestration and domain expertise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: WhatsApp's New Indian-Born Chief Faces His First Test. Delhi Just Froze His Biggest Feature.
articles.excerpt: India ordered Meta to halt WhatsApp's username feature over fraud concerns — weeks after appointing CRED founder Kunal Shah to lead the app and investing $900 million in his startup.
articles.image_caption: Kunal Shah, former CRED founder and new WhatsApp global head (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The standoff between Meta and New Delhi is a live case study in how India regulates tech products used by half a billion people — and what happens when a diaspora-connected founder takes the wheel of a global platform.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Scrapped Import Duties on Key Smartphone Parts. Apple and Xiaomi Stand to Gain.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi removed the 5–7.5 per cent levies on wireless charging modules, lithium-ion cells and display components, pushing its electronics manufacturing target to $500 billion by 2030.
articles.image_caption: North Block in New Delhi, home of India's Finance Ministry, which announced the smartphone component duty cuts (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Make in India should watch this closely — the tariff cuts strengthen the investment case for Apple's India supply chain, Indian battery startups and the broader electronics manufacturing complex.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Drafting Its First AI Law. Chatbots Get a Pass. Banks and Hospitals Do Not.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi is preparing a risk-based statute that would classify AI systems by danger level and give the government emergency powers to shut them down — a sharp reversal from its hands-off stance eight months ago.
articles.image_caption: India's Parliament — lawmakers are preparing the country's first comprehensive AI regulation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI founders, NRI investors in Indian tech, and diaspora engineers building AI products for the Indian market all need to understand this incoming regulatory framework — it could determine which AI businesses can operate freely and which face compliance costs that rival the EU's.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Xbox's Indian-American CEO Just Ordered the Biggest Restructuring in the Brand's History. The Internet Blamed Her Heritage.
articles.excerpt: Asha Sharma, born in Wisconsin, is cutting 4,800 jobs and spinning off four studios to rescue Microsoft's gaming division. Online critics turned her ethnicity into the story.
articles.image_caption: Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, at the 2026 Xbox Showcase
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American woman leads one of tech's toughest turnarounds while facing identity-based attacks — a pattern that follows diaspora professionals to the top of corporate America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Just Launched Its Biggest H-1B Fraud Investigation. Indian Tech Workers Are in the Crosshairs.
articles.excerpt: VP Vance announced dozens of subpoenas, Cognizant was named by whistleblowers, and a $100,000 application fee is in legal limbo. Here is what every Indian professional in America needs to know.
articles.image_caption: The Frances Perkins Building, headquarters of the U.S. Department of Labor in Washington, D.C., which is leading the H-1B fraud investigation
articles.nri_angle: With 71% of H-1B holders being Indian nationals, this investigation and the regulatory squeeze that follows it directly threaten the livelihoods and families of hundreds of thousands of Indian tech workers in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Broke Ground on Its Biggest AI Hub Outside America. The Location: Vizag.
articles.excerpt: Sundar Pichai's $15 billion bet on Visakhapatnam will bring gigawatt-scale compute, three subsea cables, and a new digital corridor between India and the United States.
articles.image_caption: Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai at a 2023 event
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans at Google and other Big Tech firms will work on AI systems powered by Vizag's compute. NRIs from Andhra Pradesh watch their home state become a global tech hub.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's $315 Billion IT Industry Is Staring Down Its Worst Year in a Decade. The Reckoning Has Arrived.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has cratered 28 per cent in 2026. JPMorgan sees no recovery. Nomura calls it a 'perfect storm.' And earnings season starts now.
articles.image_caption: India's IT industry, represented by major campuses in Bengaluru, faces its most challenging year in a decade (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who hold TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCLTech stocks have watched a quarter of their value evaporate. Hundreds of thousands of Indians working at these firms face slower hiring and AI-driven restructuring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World's Biggest AI Memory Chipmaker Lists on Nasdaq Tomorrow. Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Just Got Company.
articles.excerpt: SK Hynix's $28 billion offering was seven times oversubscribed. For NRI investors in the AI trade, it opens a door that was locked until now.
articles.image_caption: The Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York — SK Hynix, the world's biggest AI memory chipmaker, lists tomorrow (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American investors gain direct Nasdaq access to the dominant HBM supplier for the first time. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, one of the most prominent Indian-origin semiconductor executives, now faces his biggest rival on his home exchange.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Is About to Manufacture Its Own AI Chip. It Took Five Years to Get Here.
articles.excerpt: Code-named Iris, the custom accelerator will enter production in September as Meta races to double its computing power to 14 gigawatts and reduce its dependence on Nvidia.
articles.image_caption: Meta's headquarters in Menlo Park, California, where the company is developing its first custom AI chip (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Meta employs thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas across its AI and infrastructure teams; the shift to custom silicon reshapes career demand toward chip design, while Broadcom's Indian engineering bench and India's emerging fab ecosystem stand to benefit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia Built a CPU for AI Agents That Never Sleep. Perplexity Just Signed Up.
articles.excerpt: The Vera chip — already chosen by OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX — runs agentic AI workloads 1.5 times faster than traditional processors. Nvidia expects $20 billion in CPU sales this year.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is challenging Intel and AMD with its Vera CPU designed for the agentic AI era
articles.nri_angle: Nvidia, Intel, and AMD all run major chip design operations in Bengaluru and Hyderabad; the CPU war directly shapes career demand for thousands of Indian semiconductor engineers, while NRI investors weigh Nvidia's new revenue stream against Intel and AMD's counterattack.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Building the World's Next Great Data Centre Hub. Nobody Is Allowed to Object.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon are pouring more than $50 billion into Indian data centres. A zero-tax regime through 2047 and no public hearings are accelerating construction at a pace the West cannot match.
articles.image_caption: India is fast-tracking data centre construction to position itself as a global hub for digital infrastructure (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI professionals at Google, Microsoft, and Meta are seeing their employers become India's largest infrastructure investors, opening career transfer paths and investment opportunities in Indian data centre real estate and operations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Beat Expectations and Hired 9,300 People. Its AI Revenue Just Crossed $2.6 Billion.
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT exporter posted a 14 per cent revenue rise and its biggest quarterly hiring in three years — but the order book shrank and organic growth remains thin.
articles.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services campus in Madhapur, Hyderabad
articles.nri_angle: TCS employs tens of thousands of H-1B workers in the US; its hiring surge and AI revenue growth counter the prevailing narrative of mass layoffs hitting Indian tech professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceXAI Launches Grok 4.5 on AI's Biggest Day. It Was Trained on Tens of Thousands of Nvidia Chips.
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk's newly rebranded AI unit released its most capable model hours before OpenAI ships GPT-5.6 — and it costs a fifth of what Anthropic charges.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk, whose SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5 as its most capable AI model yet
articles.nri_angle: Indian developers and AI startups are the largest non-US user base for coding tools like Cursor; Grok 4.5's competitive pricing could reshape which frontier models Indian companies build on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-Live Can Listen and Talk at the Same Time. India's Voice AI Race Just Accelerated.
articles.excerpt: The new models enable full-duplex voice conversations — and they matter more for India's billion-phone, voice-first market than any text-based model release this year.
articles.image_caption: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, which launched GPT-Live voice models capable of simultaneous listening and speaking
articles.nri_angle: Indian developers building voice AI for the subcontinent's 22-language, voice-first market now have a commercially available full-duplex engine — but pricing and language support will determine whether it works for India-scale deployments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Space-Tech Unicorn Just Landed. A Google Founding Investor Put Up the Money.
articles.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace hits $1.1 billion after a $60 million round co-led by Ram Shriram's Sherpalo and Singapore's GIC, signalling that India's private rocket sector is ready for institutional capital.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh, India's first private rocket launch
articles.nri_angle: Ram Shriram, the Indian-American billionaire who was among Google's earliest investors, co-led the round — a signal that diaspora capital is fuelling India's deepest tech bets beyond SaaS.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Startup JPMorgan Chose Over Nvidia for AI Inference Just Raised $1 Billion.
articles.excerpt: SambaNova Systems hits $11 billion after a General Atlantic-led round, with Intel's CEO as chairman and BlackRock on the cap table. The inference chip wars are officially here.
articles.image_caption: AI inference hardware in a data center — the battleground for startups like SambaNova challenging Nvidia's dominance (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Intel — which sponsors over 2,000 H-1B workers annually — owns 9% of SambaNova, and JPMorgan, a top employer of Indian-American technologists, is its anchor customer. Cheaper inference chips could also unlock AI deployment for India's compute-starved startups.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Three Chip Plants. Now a Bengaluru Startup Wants to Design the Chips That Go Inside Them.
articles.excerpt: HrdWyr raises $13 million to build AI-native edge processors, backed by Persistent Systems and a team with 250 years of semiconductor experience from Intel, Qualcomm, and Texas Instruments.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor fabrication cleanroom — India's ambition extends from chip manufacturing to homegrown chip design (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: HrdWyr's leadership draws on semiconductor experience from Intel, Qualcomm, and TI in the US — a reverse brain drain that could put Indian-designed silicon inside consumer products used by millions of NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cisco Gave Every Worker an AI Agent. It Had Just Fired 4,000 of Them.
articles.excerpt: The networking giant is deploying one of the largest enterprise AI rollouts in history — right alongside one of its deepest rounds of layoffs. For Indian tech workers at Cisco, the message is complicated.
articles.image_caption: Cisco Systems headquarters at its San Jose, California campus
articles.nri_angle: Cisco is one of the largest H-1B employers in America; thousands of Indian engineers face both the layoff wave and the mandate to work alongside AI agents, with the 60-day visa grace period leaving no margin for error.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Half the Companies That Fired Workers for AI Will Rehire Them by 2027. The Boomerang Has Begun.
articles.excerpt: Klarna, IBM, Ford, and a growing list of corporations are quietly reversing AI-driven layoffs after discovering that chatbots cannot replace judgment, empathy, or institutional knowledge. For Indian tech workers on H-1B visas, the reversal is both lifeline and irony.
articles.image_caption: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna at SXSW 2025; his company replaced hundreds of HR workers with AI before reversing course
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders, who make up 73 per cent of visa approvals, bore the brunt of AI-driven layoffs but now stand to benefit from the rehiring wave — hybrid AI-human roles command 20-35 per cent higher salaries, and the skills Indian engineers bring are exactly what companies are realising they need.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Synopsys Just Killed the Software That Runs Chip Factories. It Wants to Design the Chips Instead.
articles.excerpt: The EDA giant told Samsung, SK Hynix, and a dozen other chipmakers their factory monitoring tools are end-of-life. AI chip design pays better — and India's 5,000 Synopsys engineers are pivoting with it.
articles.image_caption: Synopsys headquarters at 675 Almanor Avenue in Sunnyvale, California (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Synopsys employs over 5,000 engineers in Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Noida who are being reoriented from legacy analytics to AI chip design — and India's new fabs will need alternative manufacturing software.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's AI Jobs Just Grew 16 Per Cent While Overall IT Hiring Shrank. The Industry's Two-Speed Future Is Here.
articles.excerpt: New data from India's largest job portal shows AI roles surging even as the $315 billion IT sector cuts heads — a split that every NRI weighing a career move should understand.
articles.image_caption: India's technology sector is diverging into AI growth and traditional IT contraction (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The traditional IT services pipeline that moved millions of Indian engineers to the US on H-1B visas is narrowing, while AI-skilled Indians are more in demand than ever — a career-shaping divergence for NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Intel-Backed Chipmaker Just Filed to Go Public. It Thinks the AI Race Ends on Your Wrist, Not in a Data Centre.
articles.excerpt: Syntiant makes ultra-low-power AI chips for earbuds, wearables, and cars. Its Nasdaq filing arrives as Cerebras's cautionary IPO cools and India's semiconductor push targets the exact same edge market.
articles.image_caption: Syntiant designs ultra-low-power neural decision processors for edge AI applications in wearables and IoT devices (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor mission targets the same edge-device chip market that Syntiant plays in, and NRI engineers at Intel, Qualcomm, and TI work on directly competing edge AI processors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Just Cleared GPT-5.6 for the World. Here's What Indian Developers Get on Thursday.
articles.excerpt: After weeks of government testing and security reviews, OpenAI's most powerful model family goes public — with Elon Musk's Grok 4.5 crashing the party on the same day.
articles.image_caption: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, at a meeting in Washington in February 2025
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI engineers at OpenAI helped build these models, Indian startups are among the heaviest API consumers, and the new government oversight framework will shape how quickly India gets access to frontier AI.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Just Called Anthropic's Claude Code a Security Threat. Alibaba Already Banned It.
articles.excerpt: Beijing's cybersecurity authority says Claude Code secretly transmits user data to remote servers. The move deepens the US-China AI cold war — and Indian developers are caught in the crossfire.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, whose Claude Code tool has been flagged by China's cybersecurity authorities
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI engineers and startups are heavy Claude Code users; as the US-China AI war escalates, India must navigate which AI tools it can safely adopt without getting locked into either bloc's restrictions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Lost Its Biggest European Court Battle. India's Antitrust Watchdog Is Taking Notes.
articles.excerpt: The EU's General Court dismissed every Apple challenge to the Digital Markets Act. With India's own antitrust case heating up, the ruling could reshape how the App Store works for a billion users.
articles.image_caption: Apple CEO Tim Cook, whose company lost its challenge against the EU's Digital Markets Act
articles.nri_angle: Indian app developers pay Apple's 30% commission on every in-app purchase; the EU ruling could set precedent for India's CCI case that would benefit the thousands of Indian iOS developers and NRI investors holding Apple stock.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Switched On Its Third Chip Plant in Five Months. The Target: Five Billion Chips a Year.
articles.excerpt: PM Modi inaugurated CG Semi's OSAT facility in Gujarat — built with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics — as India races to have five semiconductor plants running by year-end.
articles.image_caption: A silicon wafer with semiconductor chips — the kind of component India's new OSAT facilities are designed to assemble and test
articles.nri_angle: NRIs tracking India's semiconductor ambitions now have a third plant to watch — and the sector is creating a new class of manufacturing jobs that could reshape return-to-India career calculations for chip engineers in the US and Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Landed a $1.14 Billion AI Deal With a European Giant. It's the Biggest Win in Three Years.
articles.excerpt: The Noida-based IT services firm will build an AI-driven operating model for a Fortune Global 50 company — its largest new contract since the $2.1 billion Verizon deal in 2023.
articles.image_caption: HCLTech's Noida SEZ campus — headquarters of the IT services firm that just signed its largest new deal since 2023
articles.nri_angle: For the tens of thousands of Indian engineers employed by HCLTech in the US and Europe, the deal signals that AI-led transformation — not legacy maintenance — is becoming the firm's growth engine, potentially reshaping the kinds of roles and skills the company hires for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An AI Agent Just Ran a Full Ransomware Attack on Its Own. The Cybersecurity World Is Rattled.
articles.excerpt: Sysdig researchers documented JADEPUFFER, the first known case of agentic ransomware — an LLM that breached a server, stole credentials, encrypted data, and wrote its own ransom note in 31 seconds flat.
articles.image_caption: A ransomware attack warning — AI-powered cybersecurity threats are escalating (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian cybersecurity professionals — who form a significant share of the global infosec workforce — are now confronting a threat landscape where AI agents can execute attacks faster than human defenders can respond, raising urgent questions about AI-assisted defence tools and India's own CERT-In preparedness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Beijing Is Building an Iron Curtain Around Its AI. Indian Startups Should Be Worried.
articles.excerpt: Chinese authorities are in talks with Alibaba, ByteDance and Z.ai about restricting overseas access to the country's most advanced AI models — a move that could squeeze hundreds of Indian companies built on cheap Chinese AI.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers and founders who built products on cheap Chinese AI face sudden cost pressure; India's sovereign AI efforts are years behind, leaving the diaspora-linked ecosystem exposed on both the American and Chinese fronts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Just Gave 500 Million Indians an AI Image Generator. Here's What Muse Image Does.
articles.excerpt: Muse Image, the first image-generation model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, is rolling out across Instagram Stories and WhatsApp — putting AI-powered visual creation inside apps that dominate India's digital life.
articles.image_caption: Meta's headquarters in Menlo Park, California — the company has launched its Muse AI image generator for Indian users (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers at Meta built Muse Image for the company's largest non-US market; NRI investors watching Meta's $115B AI spend should note the new subscription revenue stream targeting India's 500M WhatsApp users.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Samsung Just Posted a 19-Fold Profit Jump. Investors Dumped the Stock Anyway.
articles.excerpt: The memory chip giant's record quarter should be a celebration. Instead, a 7% share price crash signals growing fear that the AI hardware boom may be cresting — and NRI investors holding chip stocks should pay close attention.
articles.image_caption: Samsung Electronics headquarters in Suwon, South Korea — the memory chip giant's record quarter failed to reassure investors
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who loaded up on semiconductor stocks — Micron, SK Hynix, AMD, Intel — through 401(k) plans, RSUs, and brokerage accounts face a classic peak-earnings trade as Samsung's blowout quarter triggers a sector-wide selloff.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nadella, Pichai and Arora Just Bought a Cricket Team at Lord's. They Paid £145 Million.
articles.excerpt: An 11-strong consortium of Indian-origin tech billionaires has acquired a 49% stake in London Spirit, beating IPL owners in a four-hour auction that signals how Silicon Valley wealth is reshaping global cricket.
articles.image_caption: The Pavilion at Lord's Cricket Ground in London, home of London Spirit
articles.nri_angle: The CEOs who run the companies employing tens of thousands of Indian H-1B workers are now personally invested in globalising cricket — the sport that defined the NRI childhood.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DeepSeek Is Building Its Own AI Chip. Nvidia and Huawei Should Both Be Worried.
articles.excerpt: The Chinese AI lab that shocked Silicon Valley with its low-cost models is now designing a custom inference chip — a move that could reshape the semiconductor supply chain Indian engineers depend on.
articles.image_caption: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia — DeepSeek's custom chip plans threaten his company's dominance in AI inference hardware (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian-origin chip designers at Nvidia, Qualcomm, and Intel are caught in the geopolitical realignment DeepSeek's move accelerates — and India's own fab ambitions look modest by comparison.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's AI Startups Can't Buy Enough GPUs. So They're Learning to Build Without Them.
articles.excerpt: With Nvidia's newest chips locked up by hyperscalers and lead times stretching past a year, Indian AI companies are turning scarcity into a competitive advantage through radical software optimisation.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara — India's AI startups struggle to secure enough of the company's in-demand GPUs (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI engineers and investors tracking India's AI ecosystem should watch which startups survive the compute drought — they may build more resilient businesses than their better-funded Valley counterparts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sam Altman Offered Washington 5% of OpenAI. The Government Wants More.
articles.excerpt: The White House restricted GPT-5.6, lifted Anthropic's export ban, and is drafting voluntary AI standards — all in one week. Indian AI builders may feel the squeeze first.
articles.image_caption: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, in February 2025
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI startups dependent on frontier models face delays if new US release protocols add wait times; Sriram Krishnan sits at the centre of negotiations as White House AI advisor; 300,000+ Indian AI professionals in the US affected by regulatory shifts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Is Worth More Than OpenAI. Its Trillion-Dollar IPO Could Come This Fall.
articles.excerpt: Claude Code turned an AI lab into a $965 billion juggernaut. For Indian engineers with early equity and NRI investors eyeing Amazon and Alphabet, the stakes are enormous.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2023
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers at Anthropic stand to gain from IPO equity; NRI investors can access exposure through Amazon and Alphabet stakes; India's data centre industry could benefit from AI companies diversifying compute footprints.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI's Biggest Companies Are Giving Away Millions in Free Credits. Indian Founders Are Cashing In.
articles.excerpt: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are in a credit war for startup customers. For Indian-origin founders in the Valley and in Bengaluru, the free compute changes everything — for now.
articles.image_caption: The AI credit wars — Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic are giving away millions in free compute to win the next generation of developers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin founders are among the largest beneficiaries of AI credit programmes in Silicon Valley; Google's dedicated India AI fund with Accel offers $2M plus $350K in credits per startup; Indian AI companies like Sarvam AI benefit from free compute for domain-specific model training.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nadella's Microsoft Cuts 4,800 Jobs. Indian H-1B Workers Have 60 Days to Figure Out What's Next.
articles.excerpt: The biggest Xbox restructuring in history and an AI-driven headcount squeeze put thousands of visa-dependent workers on the clock.
articles.image_caption: Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft, at a company event
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft is among the top H-1B sponsors in the US; laid-off visa holders face a 60-day window to find new sponsorship or leave the country.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SK Hynix Lands on Nasdaq With a $28 Billion War Chest. Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Just Got Company.
articles.excerpt: The second-largest share sale in history brings Nvidia's biggest memory-chip supplier to American markets — right next to its Indian-origin-led rival.
articles.image_caption: The Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square — SK Hynix just became the latest Asian chipmaker to list on the exchange (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors heavily exposed to Micron now face a direct competitor on the same exchange; Micron's Gujarat fab is a major draw for Indian semiconductor engineers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Locked In Broadcom Through 2031. The Edge AI Race Has Its First Long-Term Bet.
articles.excerpt: A sweeping custom-chip deal positions Broadcom as the silicon backbone of Apple's on-device AI strategy — and creates years of design work for Indian engineers.
articles.image_caption: Apple Park in Cupertino — Apple just locked in a multibillion-dollar chip partnership with Broadcom through 2031 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Broadcom's large Indian engineering workforce in Bangalore, Hyderabad, and San Jose will drive the expanded ASIC design pipeline; NRI investors track AVGO as a diversified AI play.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Persistent Systems Just Made India's Boldest AI Bet — a $1.4 Billion Gamble on a German Software Firm
articles.excerpt: The Pune-based IT company offered a 140% premium for Munich's Nagarro, splitting Wall Street down the middle. The deal could reshape India's mid-tier tech sector — or become its most expensive mistake.
articles.image_caption: Pune — headquarters of Persistent Systems, which just announced a .45 billion acquisition of German software firm Nagarro (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Persistent employs thousands across the US and India — this acquisition tests whether Indian IT firms can compete on AI capability, not just cost, setting a precedent NRI investors and tech workers are watching closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's IT Giants Walk Into Earnings Week Facing a 'Perfect Storm.' The Numbers Already Look Bleak.
articles.excerpt: Nine brokerages warn of just 2.8% constant-currency growth as AI pricing pressure, weak client budgets, and Middle East turbulence converge. TCS reports Thursday.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bangalore — India's IT giants are heading into earnings week facing headwinds from tariffs and AI disruption (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant positions in TCS, Infosys, and Wipro through ADRs and retirement portfolios — this earnings week tests whether the sector's structural shift has a floor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wall Street Says the Real AI Money Isn't in the Magnificent Seven. It's in Memory Chips — and Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Is Leading.
articles.excerpt: UBS calls the shift 'extraordinary': AI infrastructure stocks are creating $1.4 trillion in economic value while the hyperscalers generate just $400 billion. The Indian-American CEO building a chip plant in Gujarat is at the centre of it.
articles.image_caption: Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of Micron Technology, whose bet on AI memory chips has made the company one of the decade's biggest winners
articles.nri_angle: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, born in Kanpur, is leading one of the AI era's biggest winners — and building a $2.75B chip plant in Gujarat that could create thousands of Indian engineering jobs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Is Quietly Deciding Which AI India Gets to Use. Delhi Is at the Table.
articles.excerpt: A closed-door roundtable at the 2nd Pax Silica Summit brought together Indian and American officials to negotiate semiconductor supply chains, critical minerals — and access to Anthropic's frontier models.
articles.image_caption: Jacob Helberg, US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs, who leads the Pax Silica initiative
articles.nri_angle: The US-India AI partnership shapes which frontier models Indian companies and engineers can access, affects semiconductor job creation in India, and positions Indian Americans at the nexus of the world's most consequential tech relationship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wall Street's Hottest New Trade: Betting on India Because It Missed the AI Bubble
articles.excerpt: As AI-heavy markets in South Korea and Taiwan crater, global investors are pouring back into Indian equities. The irony: India's lack of exposure to the AI trade is now its greatest selling point.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with portfolios split between US tech stocks and Indian equities are watching a historic rotation unfold — India's market resilience during the global AI selloff creates both a hedging opportunity and a rebalancing signal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Private Orbital Rocket Is Ready to Fly. The Launch Window Opens in a Week.
articles.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 — seven stories tall, carbon composite, 3D-printed engines — will attempt to reach orbit from Sriharikota as early as July 12. A $1 billion valuation says the market believes it can.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota, India's first private space launch in 2022
articles.nri_angle: For Indian aerospace engineers at SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Boeing, Skyroot represents a credible private space company in India — a career path and investment opportunity that did not exist five years ago.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foxconn Just Had Its Best Quarter in Years. India Is the Reason Wall Street Should Care.
articles.excerpt: Revenue surged 40 per cent on AI server demand, but the real story is a billion-dollar bet on Indian manufacturing — from iPhones to semiconductor packaging.
articles.image_caption: Foxconn's Dingpu manufacturing plant in Taiwan, headquarters of the world's largest contract electronics maker
articles.nri_angle: Foxconn's $1B India expansion — from iPhone assembly to semiconductor packaging — creates hardware manufacturing jobs and career paths for NRI engineers considering a return, while positioning India as a node in the global AI infrastructure supply chain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Chinese Lab Built an AI Model That Rivals Claude and GPT. It Used Zero Nvidia Chips.
articles.excerpt: Z.ai's GLM-5.2 matches frontier American models at one-sixth the cost, runs on Huawei hardware, and ships under an MIT licence. For Indian developers, it changes the maths on AI adoption.
articles.image_caption: Huawei's campus in Shenzhen — its Ascend chips power GLM-5.2, a frontier AI model built without any Nvidia hardware (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: At one-sixth the cost of US frontier models and with an MIT licence, GLM-5.2 is immediately relevant to Indian startups and IT services giants pivoting to AI — while raising geopolitical questions about India's position between US and Chinese tech ecosystems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Founder Just Bet $30 Million That Microsoft Office Needs to Be Rebuilt From Scratch
articles.excerpt: Bhavin Turakhia's Neo is an AI-native enterprise platform designed to replace, not upgrade, the workplace software stack. He's bootstrapping it himself.
articles.image_caption: Bhavin Turakhia, serial entrepreneur and founder of Neo, Zeta, and Directi
articles.nri_angle: An Indian serial entrepreneur with a $2 billion track record is taking on Microsoft and Google head-on — a signal that Indian founders are no longer limiting their ambitions to domestic or fintech plays.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TSMC Is Raising Chip Prices Again. Every Device You Own Will Feel It.
articles.excerpt: The world's dominant chipmaker is hiking 3nm prices by up to 15 per cent as AI demand overwhelms supply. Its $165 billion Arizona expansion is a year ahead of schedule.
articles.image_caption: TSMC's Fab 12B semiconductor manufacturing facility in Tainan, Taiwan
articles.nri_angle: TSMC makes the chips inside every device Indian tech workers use and invest in — from Nvidia GPUs to iPhones. The price hikes affect AI startup costs, consumer electronics, and India's own semiconductor ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Just Hired the Co-Creator of AlphaFold. It Wants to Discover Drugs, Not Just Chat.
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker is building wet labs, launching a dedicated science platform, and targeting diseases that Big Pharma won't touch. An IPO looms.
articles.image_caption: Protein structures at different scales — AlphaFold's co-creator John Jumper is joining Anthropic to apply AI prediction models to drug discovery (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India is the world's pharmacy for neglected diseases — exactly what Anthropic is targeting. Indian researchers dominate computational biology, and Anthropic's IPO is a key investment event for NRI tech investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Ransomware Gang Just Leaked Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Secrets From a Tata Factory. India Is Investigating.
articles.excerpt: The breach exposed supplier lists, component designs, and drop-test photos of unreleased iPhone models — threatening the trust at the heart of Apple's India manufacturing bet.
articles.image_caption: Apple's headquarters in Cupertino — a ransomware attack on partner Tata Electronics leaked confidential iPhone 18 Pro designs from an Indian factory
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin Apple engineers face supply chain trust fallout; NRI investors in Tata stocks now price in IP security risk as Make in India's credibility is tested.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia Doesn't Just Want to Sell You GPUs Anymore. It Wants a Cut of Your Revenue, Too.
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker's new revenue-sharing model with AI cloud providers — including India's Yotta Data Services — creates a recurring income stream while lowering the barrier for cash-strapped AI startups.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is expanding from hardware sales into recurring AI cloud revenue
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI startups gain access to Nvidia's top-tier GPUs through Yotta Data Services' inclusion in the DSX programme; NRI engineers building dual-geography AI ventures benefit from India-based compute at scale.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Big Tech Giant Wants a Data Centre in India. The Government Just Made It Tax-Free Until 2047.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft is committing $17.5 billion, Google $15 billion, and even OpenAI is scouting sites. India's data centre capacity could grow tenfold in a decade — and its zero-tax policy is the reason the world is showing up.
articles.image_caption: Server racks inside a modern data centre facility
articles.nri_angle: Pichai's Google and Nadella's Microsoft are leading the biggest infrastructure bet on India in a generation — creating thousands of high-skill jobs, investment opportunities in data centre REITs, and a new reason for NRI engineers to consider returning.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai's Google Just Admitted Its Climate Goals Are Slipping. Amazon's Numbers Are Worse.
articles.excerpt: Sustainability reports released this week show Google's emissions up 25 per cent and Amazon's up 16 per cent in a single year. The AI data centre buildout is burning through net-zero pledges faster than anyone expected.
articles.image_caption: Google server racks inside one of the company's data centres
articles.nri_angle: Pichai's Google and Jassy's Amazon are the two largest employers of Indian tech workers in the US, and both are now building massive data centres in India — raising questions about whether India's own water-stressed, coal-heavy grid can handle the AI buildout without repeating these environmental mistakes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
